# 5. Interaction Flow Based on the above functional architecture and the integration model of Agent/Copilot, this chapter focuses on how to achieve end-to-end processing of the mobile network single-domain fault management through the interaction and cooperation of agents at the Resource layer and the Service layer. ## 5.1. AN L4 Mobile Network Fault Management Interaction Flow [Figure: AN L4 Mobile Network Fault Management Interaction Flow] For faults that can be automatically repaired, the Agent operates in an autonomous closed-loop mode, without involving the FME Copilot.: Step 1 represents the fault occurrence phase. Step 2 represents the fault awareness, analysis, decision and execution phase. In the above example, the fault agent automatically performs fault identification, automatic diagnosis, and automatic repair. Step 3a represents the archiving phase. In the above example, where the resource layer agent reports the fault and the handling results to the service layer’s fault management center, which then archives the information. For faults that require on-site repairs, the fault Agent automatically performs fault identification, conducts automated diagnostics, and generates repair recommendations. The FME uses Copilot to assist humans in carrying out on-site fault handling operations. Step 1 represents the fault occurrence phase. Step 2 represents the fault awareness, analysis, and decision phase. In the above example, the fault agent automatically performs fault identification, automatic diagnosis, and automatic generate repair solution. Step 3b to 6 represent the execution phase. In the above example, the resource layer agent sends the fault and the automatically generated handling recommendations to the service layer fault center. The fault center initiates a trouble ticket system to dispatch the trouble ticket to the FME. During the on-site handling process, the FME interacts with the service layer Copilot and resource layer Copilot via an app to obtain natural language-based repair guidance. ## 5.2.
